resources.string:
CodeAssist has been rebuilt with a new on-device build system. It uses its own project configuration, so projects from a previous version aren't compatible and won't open automatically.
Back up your projects to a .zip now, your source files stay safe, and you can re-add them to a new project.

Share anonymous usage and performance data so we can see what's slow, what's failing, and which features people rely on, and fix the right things.
We collect: your app version and device model, how long builds, indexing, code completion, and previews take, build success/failure, scrubbed crash reports, how often each feature is used (for example, how many times the layout preview or Find Usages was opened), and when ads are shown or closed and changes to your ad settings.
We never collect your code, file or project names, what you type, or anything that identifies you. You can change this anytime under More while a project is open.
A real IDE. On your phone.
Write, navigate, and build Android & Java projects end to end, no laptop required.
Eclipse JDT powers precise, ranked suggestions, with signatures and docs as you type.
Edit as code, or as blocks.
Project any Java file into interlocking blocks, a live view of the same source, byte for byte.
Resolve, compile, dex, package, sign, then install straight to your phone.
One input for commands, files, and symbols, the accelerator behind everything.
Full Kotlin code completion, tuned to the same calm, ranked experience as Java.
Tag, attribute, and resource completion for Android XML with live validation.
Your projects, in a real folder.
Projects live in app storage you can open from any file manager, drop in icons, layouts, or assets, or edit from a PC. No special permissions, nothing hidden.
A faster, smoother CodeAssist, native Compose throughout, with live @Preview.
Open a project or start a new one.

settings.gradle.kts, a build.gradle.kts per module, gradle.properties, and the Gradle wrapper settings, all written from your project: modules, dependencies, SDK levels, build types, flavors and build features.

Best effort. The build files are generated from the project model rather than from a build that ran, so read them before you rely on them. Dependencies are declared as Maven coordinates and Gradle downloads them on the first sync, so that sync needs a connection.
The gradlew scripts are not included: Android Studio adds them on the first sync, or run gradle wrapper once.
These are also in GRADLE-EXPORT.md inside the archive.
